$schema_note: Seeded during spec-map.json bootstrap: every spec-current.json property/enum-member on a mapped construct (see spec-map.json) that the SDK does not yet model, excluding refund_wallet_address (added by this PR on QuoteIn -> quotes.CreateParams) and the banking_partner 'portage' member (added by this PR on BankingPartner). properties[].schema is normally a spec-current.json component schema name (matching spec-map.json's top-level 'spec' key); for a property that lives inside a types[].nested sub-object, schema is instead that nested mapping's SDK symbol name (e.g. 'TrackingPayment'), since one inline sub-object can be nested under several parent schemas (PayoutOut, PayoutOnEvmOut, and the 4 payout webhook schemas all carry the same tracking_payment shape) and the SDK symbol is the unambiguous anchor. Either way this is spec/SDK-symbol-centric, not SDK package.Type -- unlike .api-sync/contract-allowlist.json, which is keyed by SDK package.Type for cmd/contractcheck's SDK-field-centric model. cmd/apisync -check treats every entry here as satisfied regardless of spec-current.json content; removing an entry re-exposes that gap to reconciliation.

URGENT, pre-existing runtime bug found by cmd/apisync's new spec-vs-Go-type check, not introduced by this PR: the spec declares next_page as a nullable STRING cursor (example "pi_123"), but internal/types/shared.go models PaginationMetadata.NextPage as a bare int. encoding/json will fail to unmarshal any non-null next_page value on every paginated list response (customers, virtualaccounts, transfers, ...). Needs its own urgent, carefully-scoped fix -- changing an exported field's type is breaking for consumers, likely a major bump.
